mcqs.question: What is the definition of inertia?

options.A: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion
options.B: A force that changes the motion of an object
options.C: The amount of energy stored in a moving object
options.D: The speed at which an object travels

mcqs.answer: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is a property of matter that makes a body resist any change in its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. Option A states this definition correctly, while the other options describe unrelated concepts such as force, energy, or speed.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best illustrates inertia of rest?

options.A: A ball rolling down a slope continues moving
options.B: A book lying on a table stays where it is until someone pushes it
options.C: A car accelerates when the driver presses the gas pedal
options.D: A skydiver reaches a constant speed after falling for a while

mcqs.answer: A book lying on a table stays where it is until someone pushes it
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of rest means an object at rest remains at rest unless a net external force acts on it. The book on the table exemplifies this. Option A shows inertia of motion, C shows a force causing acceleration, and D involves forces like air resistance and gravity.

mcqs.question: Inertia of motion refers to:

options.A: The tendency of a moving object to continue moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by an external force
options.B: The tendency of an object at rest to stay at rest
options.C: The resistance to change in direction only, while speed may change freely
options.D: The force required to start the motion of a stationary object

mcqs.answer: The tendency of a moving object to continue moving in a straight line at constant speed unless acted upon by an external force
mcqs.explanation: Inertia of motion is the property that keeps a moving body in uniform straight‑line motion unless a net external force intervenes. Option A captures this definition. Option B describes inertia of rest, C is incorrect because inertia also resists change of direction, and D confuses inertia with the applied force.

mcqs.question: A car traveling north suddenly turns east. Which statement about inertia of direction is correct?

options.A: The car will instantly change direction without any external force
options.B: The car tends to continue moving north and a force is required to change its direction
options.C: Inertia only affects the speed of the car, not its direction
options.D: The car's mass disappears during the turn, so inertia is irrelevant

mcqs.answer: The car tends to continue moving north and a force is required to change its direction
mcqs.explanation: Inertia resists any change in the state of motion, including direction. When the car turns east, a lateral force (from the tires and road) is needed to overcome its tendency to keep moving north. Options A, C, and D are physically incorrect.

mcqs.question: Which of the following is NOT an example of inertia?

options.A: A passenger lurches forward when a bus stops suddenly
options.B: A ball rolling on a flat surface eventually comes to rest because of friction
options.C: A book remains on a shelf until you pull it out
options.D: A cyclist coasts on a level road and keeps moving without pedaling

mcqs.answer: A ball rolling on a flat surface eventually comes to rest because of friction
mcqs.explanation: Inertia is the tendency to maintain the current state of motion. Options A, C, and D illustrate objects continuing their state (moving forward, staying at rest, coasting) until an external force acts. In option B, the ball stops because friction (an external force) acts, so the stopping is not due to inertia itself.

mcqs.question: A child pushes a stationary shopping cart and it starts moving. Which statement best defines inertia in this situation?

options.A: Inertia is the tendency of the cart to resist being moved
options.B: Inertia is the force applied by the child on the cart
options.C: Inertia is the speed the cart acquires after being pushed
options.D: Inertia is the friction between the cart’s wheels and the floor

mcqs.answer: Inertia is the tendency of the cart to resist being moved
mcqs.explanation: Inertia refers to the resistance of any physical object to a change in its state of motion. The cart’s resistance to the initial push exemplifies inertia. The applied force (B), the resulting speed (C), and friction (D) are different concepts.

mcqs.question: Which statement reflects a common misconception about inertia of rest?

options.A: An object at rest will stay at rest unless a net external force acts on it
options.B: A stationary ball will start moving on its own if left alone
options.C: A book on a table remains there because of its inertia
options.D: Inertia is directly proportional to the mass of an object

mcqs.answer: A stationary ball will start moving on its own if left alone
mcqs.explanation: The misconception is that objects move spontaneously without a force. In reality, inertia of rest means the ball will stay at rest until acted upon. Option A is correct, C is a correct application, and D correctly relates inertia to mass.

mcqs.question: If a hockey puck slides on a friction‑less ice surface, why does it continue moving at constant speed?

options.A: Because its inertia makes it keep moving at the same velocity unless acted upon by a net external force
options.B: Because the puck contains a hidden engine that provides continuous thrust
options.C: Because the ice exerts a constant forward force on the puck
options.D: Because the puck’s mass decreases over time, causing acceleration

mcqs.answer: Because its inertia makes it keep moving at the same velocity unless acted upon by a net external force
mcqs.explanation: In the absence of external forces (like friction), the puck’s inertia maintains its state of uniform motion, as stated in Newton’s first law. Options B, C, and D introduce fictitious mechanisms that do not exist.
